# [BUG] Cloud start/deploy scripts update DuckDNS after Caddy already tried and failed to get a TLS cert

## Bug
Confirmed live 2026-08-20. After running `deploy-aws.sh`, the AWS backend was reachable over plain HTTP but not HTTPS. `https://lmdb-api.duckdns.org/actuator/health` failed with a TLS handshake error (`tlsv1 alert internal error`).

Root cause found via SSH + `kubectl logs caddy-tls`: `caddy-tls` starts and immediately requests a Let's Encrypt cert for `lmdb-api.duckdns.org`, but the DuckDNS record is only updated at the very end of the deploy scripts (`deploy-aws.sh`, `deploy-azure.sh`) and isn't touched at all by `start-aws.sh`/`start-azure.sh` when pods restart on instance boot. So on any fresh pod start, Caddy's ACME challenge hits the *old* cloud's IP, fails, and Caddy backs off — it does not retry immediately once DNS is fixed. Manual fix used to confirm: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/caddy-tls` after DNS is correct made it succeed instantly.

## Root Cause
Script ordering: DuckDNS update runs *after* `caddy-tls` is already up and has attempted (and failed) its ACME challenge, and nothing forces a retry afterward.

## Severity vs. Priority
**Severity (technical impact):** Major — cloud demo is unreachable over HTTPS from the Vercel frontend until someone manually restarts `caddy-tls` after DNS updates.
**Priority (business urgency):** P1

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] DuckDNS is updated before `caddy-tls` starts (or before it's given a chance to request a cert), in both deploy scripts
- [x] `start-aws.sh`/`start-azure.sh` restart `caddy-tls` after updating DuckDNS, so a stale cached failure doesn't linger after a cold start
- [x] Verified live: HTTPS health check passes with zero manual steps after a full start/deploy cycle

## Notes
Verified: `start-azure.sh` updates DuckDNS (line 114) then restarts `caddy-tls` (line 127).
